column1: # @trace order:795-5itp
# Raw frame-length decode ratchet baseline for
# scripts/check-framing-raw-decodes.sh.
# One row per file that still decodes `u32-BE` frame lengths by hand:
#   <count>\t<path>\t<disposition>
# The count is an EXACT ceiling, not an upper bound: the guard refuses a
# count above it (a new hand-rolled copy) AND a count below it (a slice
# landed and nobody tightened the ratchet). Lower the number in the same
# commit as the migration, and delete the row when the file reaches zero.
# Dispositions:
#   pending  — still to migrate onto LengthDelimitedCodec.
#   keep     — deliberate, with the reason recorded in this packet's events
#              AND at the site itself; never silently converted to pending.
# KEEP REASONS, recorded here as well as at each site (795-5itp events
# 2026-08-25T09:47:30Z and the doc comment at vsock_server.rs:1715):
#   headless/src/tray/mod.rs        — the tray control socket is a BLOCKING
#     std::os::unix::net::UnixStream held in an Arc<Mutex<Vec<..>>> subscriber
#     registry and written synchronously inside a retain; Framed needs
#     tokio AsyncRead+AsyncWrite, so this is not a swap but a move of the
#     tray control socket onto a runtime. Its bound is already the shared
#     MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES, so the duplication here is mechanics, not policy.
#     The two test sites are hand-rolled peers of that same socket.
#   headless/src/vsock_server.rs    — #[cfg(test)] interop peer. Its value is
#     being an INDEPENDENT hand-rolled decoder: delete it and "the codec
#     produces the bytes the old framing produced" becomes a tautology.
#   headless/tests/vsock_listener_e2e.rs — same, at the e2e layer.
# CLASSIFICATION OF THE LINUX-TESTABLE SITES (yoga, 2026-08-25, slice 5).
# The rows above were all filed as `pending` because the original scan counted
# DECODE SITES. Reading each one shows they are not the same kind of thing, and
# five of the six Linux-testable ones cannot migrate for reasons already
# accepted elsewhere in this packet:
#   control-wire/transport.rs:246   test peer   (inside #[cfg(test)] at :206)
#   host-shell/provisioning.rs:170  test peer   (inside #[cfg(test)] at :154)
#   host-shell/vsock_client.rs:639  test peer   (#[cfg(test)] at :402)
#   host-shell/vsock_client.rs:667  test peer   (#[cfg(all(test,unix))] at :656)
#     -- all four are independent hand-rolled decoders whose VALUE is being
#        independent; migrating them makes the interop assertion a tautology,
#        exactly as recorded for vsock_server.rs and tray/mod.rs.
#   headless/main.rs:11925          PRODUCTION but BLOCKING. `stream.read_exact`
#     with no .await -- the std UnixStream client side of the tray control
#     socket. Framed requires tokio AsyncRead+AsyncWrite; this is the same
#     blocking-stream keep already recorded for tray/mod.rs:590, seen from the
#     other end of the same socket.
# THE ONE REAL LINUX PRODUCTION TARGET -- MIGRATED, slice 6 (lenovinha,
# 2026-08-29). vm-layer/vsock_exec.rs read_envelope now decodes through
# control_frame_codec(); its row is deleted above rather than lowered to 0.
# The session is framed ONCE per entry point (`frame_stream`) and
# `&mut ExecFramed<S>` is threaded through, because the per-call Framed the
# earlier note warned about really does lose data: mutation-tested this cycle,
# `two_frames_in_one_write_are_both_read_back` FAILS under it and several
# session tests hang outright.
# THE WRITE SIDE OF THIS FILE IS A DELIBERATE KEEP, and is not counted by this
# ratchet (which scans DECODES). `write_envelope` still emits the u32-BE prefix
# itself via two staged `write_all_bounded` calls, because 690-eug2 bounds the
# length and the body SEPARATELY so a stalled writer names which half stalled;
# `SinkExt::send` encodes and writes in one call and cannot. It writes through
# `Framed::get_mut()`, which is sound only because the Sink half is never used,
# so the codec write buffer is always empty. Pinned by
# `a_peer_that_stops_draining_does_not_park_the_writer`.
